recipes.name: Turf n' Turf inspired by Parks and Rec
instructions: for the PorterHouse Steak

Place the steak on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet. Cover with a generous sprinkling of kosher salt and let sit for at least 1 hour. If feeling adventurous, leave it in the fridge uncovered overnight. - 24 oz PorterHouse steak - Kosher salt
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy cast iron pan over high heat for about 5 minutes, until smoking. - Vegetable oil

Pat the porterhouse as dry as humanly possible and place it into the cast iron pan. Let cook for about 2 minutes, until a deep brown, robust crust has formed on the first side. Give it a flip and repeat the process on the opposite side.
If interested in trying the steak alla fiorentina, kill the heat and place the steak on the fatty side and sear. Then stand the steak upright on its bone.
Place the steak (still upright) into a 450°F oven. Wait until the thickest part of the steak reaches an internal temperature of 120°F.
Once the steak has reached the internal temperature of 120°F, plate and let rest for 10 minutes.
To cut steakhouse style, remove the strip and filet mignon from the bone. Then slice and plate.
for the T-Bone Steak

Place the steak on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet. Cover with a generous sprinkling of kosher salt and let sit for at least 1 hour. If feeling adventurous, leave it in the fridge uncovered overnight. - T 16oz Bone steak - Kosher salt
Heat vegetable oil in a carbon steel pan over high heat until smoking. - Vegetable oil

Pat the steak as dry as humanly possible and place it into the cast iron pan. Let cook for about 2 minutes, until a deep brown, robust crust has formed on the first side. Give it a flip and repeat the process on the opposite side.
Add cloves of crushed garlic, a few sprigs of rosemary and thyme, and butter to the pan. - 3 cloves crushed garlic - 5 tbsp unsalted butter - Rosemary sprigs - Thyme sprigs
Once the butter is melted, tip the pan towards the garlic and herbs and baste the steak with the hot herb butter. Do this until the thickest part of the steak registers at 125°F.
Plate the steak and bathe it one last time with the herby, garlicky, brown butter.
Let rest for at least 10 minutes before serving.
for the Mashed Potatoes

Peel Yukon gold potatoes and cut them into equally-sized pieces. Place into a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and cook for at least 20 minutes, or until completely tender (a paring knife cuts through with no issue). - 7 Yukon gold potatoes (about 3lbs)
Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot over medium-low heat. Cook and stir them around for about 1 minute.

Kill the heat and add about half & half and unsalted butter. Mash together until mostly mashed, then season liberally with kosher salt and white pepper. - ½ cup half & half - 5 tbsp unsalted butter - Kosher salt - White pepper
Mash them up the rest of the way and taste for seasoning and consistency.
Cover and keep warm until ready to serve.
